task.title: Setting Up Git For Your New Project
task.shortdesc: How to complete the initial Git setup for a project.

context.p: These steps cover installing Git and initializing your first repository.

step.cmd: Install Git on your Linux system.
step.info: If you are using a Debian based distro, run the command: sudo apt-get update then: sudo apt install git-all If you are using a Red Hat based distro, use the command: sudo dnf update followed by: sudo dnf install git-all

step.cmd: Configure your user name and email.

info.p: To set your username, run the command: git config --global user.name "Random User"
To set your email, run the command: git config --global user.email randomuser@test.com To check your personal settings, run the command git config --list

step.info: If you already have a project, navigate to the relevant folder, then initialize an empty repository with the command: git init
To clone an existing repository, type the command: git clone 'URL'

Git will not begin tracking your files unless you add them. To add all the files in your directory to Git, type the command: git add -A To add a single file called 'foo', type the command: git add foo

To commit your changes with a message, type the command: git commit -m "Initial commit for Git's documentation project" if you do not insert a commit message at the time of committing your files (i.e. if you only type `git commit`), Git will launch the default text editor set in your environment variables.

result.p: Your project is now a Git repository, staged and ready for your first tracked commit.
